faults.fault: explanation skipping (here, getting wrong) the causal step
faults.finding: "Past half a turn the flux builds through the coil from the other side, so the emf pushes the other way" puts the reversal at edge-on (90°). The emf follows the change in the flux: shrinking one way (0° to 90°) and building the other way (90° to 180°) are the same change, so the emf keeps one direction for the whole half turn from face-on to face-on and reverses as the coil passes face-on, where the change turns round. The interactive's description already had this right; the text contradicted it.
faults.fix: Say the shrinking-then-building is one change, so the push keeps its direction from face-on to face-on and reverses at face-on.

faults.fault: false absolutes / a source's qualifier lost
faults.finding: "60 for most ships' supplies" turns the source's "the most common frequency adopted for use on board ship" into a majority claim the quote does not make.
faults.fix: "60 Hz, the most common frequency on board ship".

faults.fault: recommended shape: one fully worked example with real numbers computed from the rule
faults.finding: The explanation states N × B × A × ω but never works a number from it; the only numbers worked are in the practice and the puzzles.
faults.fix: Work the picture's own coil: 100 × 0.5 × 0.01 × 2π × 1 = 3.14 V peak, 1.57 V at 30° past face-on, and 6.28 V with a 0.5 s period at twice the speed.

faults.finding: "the share of the coil square to the field" is hard to picture; B is named without its unit in explain.
faults.fix: "how much of the coil's face the field lines meet", and B named as the field strength in teslas.

faults.fault: a DO screen with a weak distractor
faults.finding: "The coil's direction of turning" is not a mistake anyone makes. The real slips are that the current stops for half a turn, or that the magnet's field itself alternates.
faults.fix: Options: the direction of the push and of the current; the field between the poles; nothing, the current stops for half of each turn. Each wrong one gets its own hint.

faults.fault: a claim that could mislead in the dossier
faults.finding: "Peak 120 V at 60 turns a second" is true of this simple coil with a fixed field, but a real generator is run to hold its voltage. The Why? must say so, or Dan may think ship supplies are higher voltage because of 60 Hz.
faults.fix: Why? adds that real generators adjust their field to hold the voltage, which Three-phase power systems at sea takes up.

faults.finding: Paragraph 3 carries the sine, the reversal, the frequency and the peak rule at once.
faults.fix: Keep four paragraphs: overview; flux and emf; why a sine and what alternates; what sets the size, with the worked numbers, the puzzle link and the takeaway.

passes: Text teaches the idea rather than talking about it; the idea is named in the first two sentences.
The brief names the cause (flux changing fastest) and the effect (emf peak), and face-on shows the cause absent (most flux, no emf).
Every number is a control, computed, assumed and worded as an example, or cited; the 60 Hz fact is cited and used as an example only.
No recall checks (read mode); the DO screens ask him to reason on the picture.
Misconception shown failing: face-on has the most flux and zero emf; what alternates is a DO screen with its own hints.
Analogy from the sea reproduces the main result (flow follows rate of change of level) and says where it breaks.
Nothing re-teaches the sine, amplitude, period or ω from Trigonometry; they are used with a reminder.
